strengths: Formulating outdoor weather manipulation in intrinsic space (decomposing into albedo, normal, roughness, metallicity, and irradiance) is well-motivated and physically principled, avoiding typical pixel-level hallucinatory artifacts.

The Intrinsic Map-Aware Attention (IMAA) mechanism elegantly leverages DINOv2 features and learnable map embeddings to guide DiT attention towards relevant geometric and material features, demonstrated to improve intrinsic estimation quality.

The paper contributes valuable data resources, WeatherSynthetic (38k paired synthetic scenes with ground-truth intrinsics under varied weather) and WeatherReal (18k pseudo-labeled real-world scenes), which help bridge the gap in outdoor driving intrinsic datasets.

Strong experimental evaluation spanning multiple benchmarks (ACDC, Waymo, TransWeather) showing consistent quantitative gains over inverse rendering baselines (RGB<->X, IID, DiffusionRenderer) and qualitative improvements over generic editing methods (Flux-Kontext, Qwen-Image-Edit).

Downstream validation on autonomous driving tasks (DETR detection and Segformer segmentation on ACDC) clearly illustrates the practical utility and robustness benefits of the proposed decomposition and weather normalization.
weaknesses: The evaluation of inverse rendering on real-world datasets is largely qualitative (Fig. 9); quantitative decomposition benchmark results in Tab. 3 are restricted to the synthetic dataset WeatherSynthetic, leaving the exact numerical fidelity on real-world distributions less thoroughly validated.

The construction of WeatherReal relies on pseudo-labels generated by the inverse renderer itself combined with MLLM filtering and Flux-Kontext editing, which could potentially introduce circular bias or model-induced priors during fine-tuning.

The framework operates strictly on single frames and currently does not enforce temporal consistency, which is an important consideration for real-world autonomous driving video sequences as acknowledged in Section 4.5.

strengths: Compelling conceptual motivation: Operating in intrinsic space (decoupling geometry, invariant materials, and weather-variant illumination) addresses key failure modes of pixel-space editing methods, such as hallucinating objects or unintentionally altering car/scene colors.

Valuable dataset contribution: Constructing WeatherSynthetic (38k UE5 scenes with rich weather variations and ground-truth intrinsic maps) and WeatherReal helps address the acute scarcity of paired outdoor intrinsic datasets for autonomous driving scenarios.

Meaningful downstream evaluation: The paper convincingly demonstrates that intrinsic-space weather editing and restoration directly benefit downstream perception tasks, showing substantial quantitative gains on object detection (DETR) and semantic segmentation (Segformer) on the adverse-weather ACDC benchmark.

Strong experimental validation: Extensive comparisons across pixel-space image editing methods, weather restoration methods, and neural rendering baselines demonstrate consistent quantitative and qualitative improvements.
weaknesses: Architectural clarity of the inverse renderer: Section 3 lacks explicit details on how Stable Diffusion 3.5 is configured to predict multiple intrinsic maps (e.g., whether all channels/maps are predicted jointly via concatenated latent channels, sequentially, or through multi-task heads).

Simplicity and potential issues with CLIP text interpolation: The text interpolation relies on unconstrained linear shifting in CLIP embedding space ($E = Embed(w_{base}) + \alpha \cdot e$). Because CLIP space geometry is hyperspherical, linear interpolation often yields out-of-distribution embeddings unless normalized or handled via spherical interpolation (slerp).

Self-reinforcing bias in WeatherReal: The WeatherReal dataset relies on the model's own inverse renderer for pseudo-labels and Flux-Kontext for weather manipulation, which risks compounding generative hallucinations and bias during fine-tuning.

Lack of temporal consistency for driving: While properly acknowledged in the limitations, autonomous driving datasets are fundamentally video-based. The single-image formulation exhibits noticeable temporal jitter across frames as shown in Figure 12.

strengths: Sound and well-motivated framework: Operating weather manipulation within intrinsic space (disentangling material, geometry, and lighting/weather) addresses a fundamental flaw in pixel-space generative editing, notably the preservation of scene structure and physical plausibility.

Significant empirical gains on downstream driving perception: The paper demonstrates tangible utility for autonomous driving, showing substantial metric improvements on the ACDC benchmark for object detection (DETR AP75 from 13.15% to 24.60%) and semantic segmentation (SegFormer mIoU from 24.13% to 30.05%) when adverse weather is edited to clear conditions.

Valuable dataset contribution: WeatherSynthetic (38k UE5 driving frames with full intrinsic maps across 7 weather conditions) and WeatherReal provide a much-needed benchmark and training resource for outdoor autonomous driving inverse/forward rendering.

Extensive comparative evaluations: The submission thoroughly benchmarks against multiple paradigms, including pixel-space editing (Flux-Kontext, Qwen-Image-Edit, WeatherWeaver), weather restoration (AWRaCLe, Histoformer), and diffusion-based intrinsic decomposition (RGB<->X, IID, GeoWizard, DiffusionRenderer).
weaknesses: Architectural and conditioning details in the main text are underspecified: The manuscript does not clearly explain how the multi-channel intrinsic maps (albedo, normal, roughness, metallicity) are fed into the forward renderer DiT backbone (e.g., channel concatenation, ControlNet-style cross-attention, or latent modulation).

Missing specifics on Intrinsic Map-Aware Attention (IMAA): In Section 3.2, Eq. (3)-(5) define an attention bias matrix derived from DINOv2 tokens and map embeddings, but the paper omits crucial details regarding the spatial resolution alignment between DINOv2 patch tokens and SD 3.5 DiT latent tokens, as well as the heuristic-guided progressive training strategy.

Risk of error propagation in WeatherReal: The WeatherReal dataset relies on the proposed inverse renderer itself to generate pseudo-ground-truth intrinsic maps and an external pixel-space editor (Flux-Kontext) to produce weather variations. More quantitative validation is needed to demonstrate that this pseudo-labeling pipeline does not inject systematic artifacts into the forward renderer training.

Evaluation on downstream label alignment: When transforming adverse weather scenes into sunny conditions for ACDC evaluation, generative models can introduce slight spatial shifts or object hallucination. While overall AP/mIoU increases, an explicit analysis of mask/box spatial drift or false positive generation would strengthen the claim of downstream reliability.
